name: United Arab Emirates
tagline: Western degrees in the Gulf, admitted on four calendars months apart
summary: The UAE is a shopping centre of imported universities, almost all of them teaching in English. Dubai's academic free zones host British, Australian, Indian and American campuses awarding their home degrees; Abu Dhabi hosts NYU and the Sorbonne. Teaching is in English almost everywhere, the IB is read as a matter of routine, and the academic calendar is American — apply in the autumn, start in August or September. One institution stands out and deserves separate consideration: NYU Abu Dhabi, which awards all its aid to non-Emirati students on financial need rather than merit and renews it at the same level each year. Against a 2026-27 cost of attendance of USD 90,434, that aid decides whether it is an option at all.
whyConsider: NYU Abu Dhabi awards need-based financial aid to non-Emirati students, assessed on the CSS Profile and renewed at the same level each year. Its 2026-27 cost of attendance is USD 90,434, so the aid decides whether it is affordable.
Dubai's branch campuses award the home institution's degree — a Heriot-Watt, Birmingham, Wollongong or Middlesex degree, recognised in Europe, obtained in the Gulf.
Everything is taught in English and the IB is a standard entry qualification throughout.
The American calendar suits IB students: applications in the autumn and early winter, decisions in the spring, start in August.
No income tax, a large and young international population, and flight connections to everywhere — Copenhagen is around seven hours.

NYU Abu Dhabi awards all its financial aid to non-Emirati students on need, assessed on the CSS Profile and renewed at the same level each year. Against a 2026-27 cost of attendance of USD 90,434, that aid decides whether it is affordable at all.

A branch campus awards the home institution's degree — a Heriot-Watt, Birmingham, Wollongong or Middlesex degree, recognised in Europe, obtained in the Gulf — and Birmingham Dubai states that it applies the same entry requirements as its UK campus.

An application to a UK university's Dubai campus does not go through UCAS and does not use one of your five UCAS choices. Birmingham Dubai charges nothing for it either. It costs a student almost nothing to hold alongside a UK application.
Several institutions here still accept applications after IB results are released on 6 July.
watchOuts: The UAE is four admissions environments wearing one flag, and the difference between them is months. NYU Abu Dhabi closes on 1 November 2026 for a 2027 start. RIT Dubai will still take an application on 22 August 2027. Heriot-Watt Dubai will take one three weeks before term. Get this wrong in either direction and you either miss the option or spend a year assuming you have more time than you do.

A branch campus is not the parent university with better weather. It is licensed separately by MoHESR through the Commission for Academic Accreditation and, in Dubai, permitted by KHDA, and it teaches a subset of the parent’s programmes with its own staff. What it does share is the degree and, at Birmingham Dubai explicitly, the entry requirements. Check both before assuming either.

A Dubai campus application does not go through UCAS and does not use one of your five UCAS choices. Birmingham Dubai says so in terms. That is an advantage worth knowing about, and it is also why a UK branch campus will not appear anywhere in your UCAS planning.

Nine of the fourteen institutions here have not published a 2027 date at all. Four say so explicitly and five simply do not publish one. Either way, re-check each university's page in autumn 2026, as the calendar entries below say.

Every foreign school certificate needs attestation by the local education authority and an equivalency certificate from the UAE Ministry of Education. Khalifa University states that applications with missing documents will not be accepted. This is slow and it is not optional.
Tuition figures are given here only for NYU Abu Dhabi and Khalifa. Check every other fee on the university’s own page.

Whether NYU Abu Dhabi is formally need-blind for international applicants is not stated on its own pages. What is confirmed is that all financial aid grants for non-Emirati citizens are need-based; the only named merit scholarship is reserved for Emirati nationals. Ask admissions directly whether your financial need affects the admission decision.

NYU Abu Dhabi is very selective: NYU's own figures for autumn 2022 entry show it admitted 5% of more than 18,700 applicants, with an IB median of 40 (38 to 41 between the 25th and 75th percentiles). Its Early Decision rounds are binding. You are released from that agreement only if the aid package will not let you attend.

The federal universities are not really open to you. UAEU and Zayed direct places and subsidies at UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers, who apply through a national placement route, and run international admission as a separate and much smaller stream. Establish eligibility before investing effort.

The UAE is socially conservative by European standards. Laws on alcohol, relationships outside marriage and public behaviour differ from what you are used to, and enforcement varies by emirate. Read your own foreign ministry’s travel advice properly, not the marketing brochures.
Summer heat in Dubai and Abu Dhabi is extreme — 45°C is routine in July and August — and outdoor life effectively stops for three months.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA: check su.dk before budgeting. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance funds a full degree outside Europe.

Treating the UAE as one deadline is the main mistake to avoid. Its institutions are eight months apart: NYU Abu Dhabi's Early Decision I closes 1 November 2026 for a 2027 start, and RIT Dubai's Fall 2027 deadline is 22 August 2027. Nine of the fourteen institutions here have published no 2027 date at all, and the calendar says for each one whether that is because the university said the date is coming or because it published nothing.

A branch campus is not the parent university with better weather. It is licensed separately — nationally by the Commission for Academic Accreditation under MoHESR, and in Dubai by KHDA, in Abu Dhabi by ADEK — and teaches a subset of the parent's programmes with its own staff. What it does share is the degree, and sometimes the entry requirements. Check both rather than assuming either.

Every foreign school certificate needs attestation by the local education authority and then an equivalency certificate from the UAE Ministry of Education. Khalifa University states that applications with missing documents will not be accepted. This is slow and it is not optional.

The federal universities are not really open to you. UAEU and Zayed University direct places and subsidies at UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers, who apply through a national placement route, and run international admission as a separate and much smaller stream. Establish eligibility before investing effort.
NYU Abu Dhabi's Early Decision rounds are binding. You are released from the agreement only if the financial aid package will not let you attend — not because a better offer arrives.
Tuition figures are given here only for NYU Abu Dhabi and Khalifa. Read every other fee off the university's own page.

The UAE is socially conservative by Danish and most European standards. Laws on alcohol, relationships outside marriage and public behaviour differ from those in Denmark and most of Europe, and enforcement varies by emirate. Read your own foreign ministry's travel advice properly, not the marketing brochures.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA: check su.dk before budgeting. If you cannot claim it, check your own country's student finance rules for a full degree outside Europe.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: There is no national minimum. Two institutions publish one: Khalifa University requires the full Diploma with a minimum of 4 in each of six HL/SL subjects and a total of 24 points, and RIT Dubai requires 28 points for engineering and 24 for computing, business, psychology and new media design. Minimums for the other institutions here are not known, and neither figure applies to any other institution.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set by each institution, not nationally. Khalifa University requires English, Mathematics and one science among the six subjects, depending on the programme, and excludes Islamic Studies from them. RIT Dubai requires Mathematics, Physics and one of Chemistry or Biology at grade 4 or above for engineering. Branch campuses apply the parent university’s subject rules — Birmingham Dubai states that it upholds the same entry requirements as its UK campus.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. UAE institutions read IB points directly. What they do require, and what no European system asks for, is an equivalency certificate for the Diploma issued by the UAE Ministry of Education, on top of attestation of the transcript by the local education authority — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah.
notes: The IB is standard currency here — the UAE has many IB World Schools, so admissions offices read the transcript fluently.

Khalifa University also grants advanced standing credit for a score of 6 or higher on certain HL subjects, which can shorten the degree. It does not grant credit for lower scores, and if an exam is taken twice the higher score counts.

RIT Dubai places students into English courses by IB English grade rather than by test: 7 and 4–6 both reach its highest writing course, 3 reaches the one below. That is a useful case of an institution publishing how it actually reads an IB subject grade.

Branch campuses generally apply the same IB requirements as the home institution, which makes their entry standards easy to look up on the parent university’s site — and means the parent’s site, not the Dubai one, is the page to trust.

The Commission for Academic Accreditation licenses institutions and accredits programmes nationally; KHDA licenses and certifies degrees in Dubai and ADEK in Abu Dhabi. Check that your programme appears on the accredited list if you intend to use the degree in the Gulf.
Minimum IB scores for the other twelve institutions are not given here. Ask them directly; an unpublished minimum is not proof that there is none.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Essentially all of them. English is the medium of instruction across the private and branch-campus sector and at NYU Abu Dhabi, Khalifa and the American University of Sharjah. Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi teaches mostly in French, with three bachelor's degrees in English.
language.englishProof: IB English is normally accepted. Some institutions require IELTS or TOEFL regardless of the IB, so check each one.
notes: Arabic is the official language but English is the working language of the country, and in Dubai you can live for years without needing Arabic.
Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi is the exception: it delivers French university programmes and most of its teaching is in French, with a French-language preparatory year available.
Federal institutions such as UAE University and Zayed University teach some programmes in Arabic — check the medium of instruction.

feeContext.summary: The UAE does not recognise EU or EEA status and gives it no advantage. The categories that exist are UAE national, resident and international, and an EU/EEA student applying from Denmark is in the last. See the non-EU row.

Two figures are given here. NYU Abu Dhabi's 2026-27 cost of attendance is USD 90,434, of which tuition is USD 68,574 — before need-based aid. Khalifa University charges AED 2,500 per credit hour, which its own page puts at roughly AED 81,250 a year at 12–16 credits, with campus housing at AED 10,000–20,000 per semester. Other fees are not given here, and these do not apply to any other institution.

sectorLandscape.summary: The UAE's higher education divides by who owns and licenses the institution, not by where it is. Three kinds dominate and they behave completely differently: federal institutions built for Emirati nationals, UAE-owned private universities awarding their own degrees, and branch campuses of foreign universities awarding the parent's. Behind all three sits a licensing layer rather than an admissions one — the Commission for Academic Accreditation licenses nationally under MoHESR, KHDA licenses and certifies degrees in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi — and the free zones such as Dubai International Academic City and Dubai Knowledge Park are where the branch campuses physically sit. There is no national admissions authority at all, which is why there are four routes and no portal.

routes.what: United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain and Zayed University in Abu Dhabi and Dubai. Government-owned, heavily subsidised, and built to educate Emirati nationals — places and money go to nationals and children of Emirati mothers first, who apply through a national placement route a foreign applicant cannot use. International admission exists as a separate and much smaller stream that you contact the university about directly.
routes.note: Neither publishes an undergraduate deadline for 2027. Zayed says its dates are to be confirmed; UAEU says applications happen during announced periods and announces none.

routes.what: Rarely mentioned to foreigners: a federal network of seven colleges across Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Al Dhafra, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, awarding applied diplomas and bachelor's degrees across around forty programmes. It is the UAE's nearest equivalent to a Danish erhvervsakademi — shorter, vocational, employer-facing — and it rarely appears in English-language guides to studying in the Gulf.
routes.note: HCT runs an international student portal, so it is not closed to foreign applicants. What the IB buys you there, and what it costs, are not known; ask HCT. A student who would suit it may not otherwise hear of it.

routes.what: UAE-owned, fee-paying institutions licensed by the Commission for Academic Accreditation and awarding their own degrees — Khalifa University, the American University of Sharjah, the American University in Dubai, Canadian University Dubai. Several are American or Canadian in structure and accreditation without being anyone's branch campus, which is a distinction worth holding onto: the degree is theirs, not an imported one.
routes.note: These are the institutions whose 2027 dates are least likely to be published yet and the ones to re-check from autumn 2026. Khalifa is a research university that admits by competitive test; the others are more accessible.

routes.englishName: branch campus of a foreign university
routes.what: A foreign university operating a campus in a UAE free zone and awarding its home degree: Heriot-Watt Dubai, University of Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, the University of Wollongong in Dubai, RIT Dubai, SP Jain Dubai, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi. The degree, and often the entry requirements, come from the parent — Birmingham Dubai states it applies the same entry requirements as its UK campus, and Heriot-Watt lets students move between its Dubai, Edinburgh and Malaysia campuses mid-degree. The dates, the fees and the visa come from the UAE campus.
routes.note: You apply directly to the campus, not through UCAS, and a Dubai application does not use one of your five UCAS choices. Most of these publish no deadline at all; Heriot-Watt Dubai publishes a policy instead, saying it admits on a rolling basis up to three weeks before term.

routes.what: Institutions owned by or built around a single national employer or sector — aviation, hospitality, security, energy — training directly into it. They sit outside the university listings and outside most guidance, and they are a real route for a student who already knows the industry they want.
routes.note: No institution of this kind is listed on this page, and entry, cost and IB access are not covered here.

The University of Birmingham Dubai is licensed by MoHESR through the Commission for Academic Accreditation and separately permitted by KHDA, and states that it upholds the same entry requirements as its UK campus.

The Higher Colleges of Technology is the UAE's largest higher education institution, a federal network of seven colleges across Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Al Dhafra, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, awarding applied diplomas and bachelor's degrees across around forty programmes, and it operates an international student admissions portal.

jurisdictions.name: NYU Abu Dhabi — admitted through NYU
jurisdictions.summary: One institution, and its own jurisdiction because nothing else in the UAE works like it. NYU Abu Dhabi is one of NYU's three degree-granting campuses and admits through the Common Application on the American calendar, with two binding Early Decision rounds and a Regular Decision that closes on 5 January — six months before IB results.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: 1 November, 1 January and 5 January, all 23:59 EST, with decisions on 15 December, 15 February and 1 April. The two Early Decision rounds are binding. NYUAD publishes these dates without a year, so the years are expected rather than confirmed.

sources.title: NYU Abu Dhabi runs three rounds with application deadlines of 1 November, 1 January and 5 January, all at 23:59 EST, with decisions on 15 December, 15 February and 1 April, and CSS Profile financial aid deadlines of 10 November, 10 January and 1 February.

variations.label: Cost and aid
variations.summary: 2026-27 cost of attendance USD 90,434, of which tuition is USD 68,574. All financial aid grants to non-Emirati citizens are need-based, and aid offered at admission is normally renewed at the same level; NYUAD does not state on its current pages that it meets full need. The CSS Profile is a separate application with its own deadline.

sources.title: NYU Abu Dhabi's institutional grant aid for non-Emiratis is need-based, assessed on the CSS Profile, and renewed at the level offered on admission provided the student stays full-time, keeps a GPA of at least 2.0 and earns credit in at least 75 per cent of attempted hours.

NYU Abu Dhabi runs three rounds with application deadlines of 1 November, 1 January and 5 January, all at 23:59 EST, with decisions on 15 December, 15 February and 1 April, and CSS Profile financial aid deadlines of 10 November, 10 January and 1 February.

Early Decision at NYU Abu Dhabi is binding: an admitted student with an adequate financial aid package must withdraw other applications and accept within two to three weeks, and is released from the agreement only if the aid package will not let them attend.

jurisdictions.name: Branch campuses admitting on their own calendar
jurisdictions.summary: Foreign universities' UAE campuses that run their own admissions: Heriot-Watt Dubai, Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, the University of Wollongong in Dubai, RIT Dubai, SP Jain Dubai and Sorbonne Abu Dhabi. The degree and usually the entry requirements come from the parent; the dates, the fees and the visa come from the campus. You apply directly and not through UCAS.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Only RIT Dubai publishes dates: Early phase 15 January, Regular 31 May, deadline 22 August, with late applications reviewed on space availability. Heriot-Watt Dubai publishes a policy instead — rolling, up to three weeks before term. Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, UOWD and SP Jain Dubai publish no application deadline at all. Sorbonne Abu Dhabi has published 2026 and not 2027.

sources.title: RIT Dubai is accepting applications for Fall 2027, with an Early Admission Phase until 15 January, a Regular Admission Phase until 31 May and an application deadline of 22 August, after which applications are reviewed on space availability. Its IB minimum is 28 points for engineering and 24 for computing, business, psychology and new media design.

Heriot-Watt University Dubai runs rolling year-round admissions with every programme taking a September intake, accepts applications up to three weeks before an intake starts, and expects most applicants six to ten months ahead.

variations.label: Visas
variations.summary: Birmingham Dubai sets a separate, harder deadline for new international students to apply for a University-sponsored visa from outside the UAE — 24 August 2026 for the September 2026 intake. For an applicant living in Denmark this, not the application, is the binding date, and the 2027 one is not yet published.

sources.title: Birmingham Dubai sets a deadline for new international students to apply for a University-sponsored visa from outside the UAE: 24 August 2026 for the September 2026 intake and 14 December 2026 for the January 2027 intake, with express options a week later in each case. No date is published for the September 2027 intake.

Applications to the University of Birmingham's Dubai campus are made directly through the University's own admissions portal, not through UCAS, do not count towards a UCAS applicant's five choices, carry no application fee, may be made on predicted grades, and receive a decision within ten working days. No application deadline is published.

The University of Birmingham Dubai is licensed by MoHESR through the Commission for Academic Accreditation and separately permitted by KHDA, and states that it upholds the same entry requirements as its UK campus.

jurisdictions.name: UAE private universities
jurisdictions.summary: UAE-owned institutions licensed by the Commission for Academic Accreditation and awarding their own degrees: Khalifa University, the American University of Sharjah, the American University in Dubai and Canadian University Dubai. Each admits directly on its own calendar, and no two of those calendars agree.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: AUS opens Fall 2027 on 19 October 2026 and sets Early File Completion on 5 July 2027 — the day before IB results — but publishes no closing date for Fall. Khalifa says its Fall 2027 timeline is still to come. Canadian University Dubai publishes one academic year at a time and sets international deadlines about a week ahead of domestic ones. The American University in Dubai publishes month ranges rather than dates.

sources.title: For Fall 2027 the American University of Sharjah opens applications on 19 October 2026 and sets Early File Completion on 5 July 2027, with classes starting 23 August 2027. It publishes no closing date for Fall 2027, although it publishes one for Spring 2027 and one for Summer 2027.
Khalifa University has closed Fall 2026 undergraduate admissions and has not yet published a Fall 2027 application timeline.

Canadian University Dubai publishes admission deadlines for the 2026-27 academic year only, with separate and earlier dates for international applicants: Fall 21 August 2026, Spring 3 January 2027 and Summer 12 May 2027 for international students, against 27 August 2026, 8 January 2027 and 19 May 2027 for domestic ones.

The American University in Dubai publishes application periods as month ranges rather than dates: for the Fall semester, early applications up until March/April and late applications through July/August, with open admissions in the summer terms.

variations.label: Cost
variations.summary: Khalifa University publishes AED 2,500 per credit hour, which it puts at roughly AED 81,250 a year at 12–16 credits, plus AED 10,000–20,000 per semester for campus housing, and includes any scholarship in the admission offer rather than in a separate application. Fees for the other three are not given here.

Khalifa University has closed Fall 2026 undergraduate admissions and has not yet published a Fall 2027 application timeline.

jurisdictions.name: Federal institutions
jurisdictions.summary: United Arab Emirates University and Zayed University. Government-owned and built for Emirati nationals, who reach them through a national placement route a foreign applicant cannot use. International admission is a separate, smaller stream handled directly by the university, and neither institution publishes an undergraduate deadline for 2027.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Zayed University's undergraduate application page says "Application Dates to be confirmed". UAEU says applicants apply through the ministry's portal during announced application periods and publishes no undergraduate period — although it does publish graduate ones.

UAEU admits undergraduates competitively within each college's capacity through its own online portal, routes international students separately from UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers, and publishes no undergraduate application deadline.

notes: Grouping decision. institutionGrouping is "jurisdiction" with four jurisdictions each of kind "sector", rather than the "sector" grouping. The distinction is not cosmetic: what divides UAE institutions is not where they are but who licenses them and whose calendar they admit on, and each of those divisions has its own Application Route, its own dates and its own cost story — which is what an Application Jurisdiction is for and what the sector grouping, which carries no route, is not. Grouping by emirate would have put Birmingham Dubai next to Middlesex Dubai and away from Birmingham UK, which is the wrong way round.

NYU Abu Dhabi is a branch campus and is still its own jurisdiction. It admits through NYU's system on the American calendar, with a binding Early Decision closing 1 November — eight months before anything else recorded here. Leaving it in the branch-campus group would have rebuilt exactly the lump this pass was opened to dissolve.

Every NYU Abu Dhabi and RIT Dubai date is provisional. Both publish bare recurring days with no year, so the 2027 years are inferred. NYUAD's Early Decision I falls on 1 November 2026 on that inference, five weeks after this record was written, and needs confirming before anyone acts on it.

Not established: tuition for twelve of the fourteen institutions; minimum IB points for twelve of the fourteen; whether NYU Abu Dhabi is need-blind for international applicants; whether the federal universities charge international students differently or cap the international stream; whether any branch campus runs a different process for an applicant living outside the UAE beyond the visa step; work rights on a student residence visa, which are not re-verified from an official source here.
Programme-level records not yet created. Stages 1–5 of the research brief are done for this Destination; stage 6 is not.

2026-09-24 audit: the claim that NYU Abu Dhabi "meets demonstrated need" was removed wherever it appeared. NYUAD's current financial-aid, cost and application pages say its aid for non-Emiratis is need-based and renewed at the same level, and say nothing about meeting full need. Sorbonne Abu Dhabi's English-taught bachelor's degrees are now named from its own page.

portal.name: No central portal. The UAE has four admissions environments and which one you are in decides everything about how and when you apply: federal institutions, UAE private universities, and branch campuses of foreign universities — and, on its own, NYU Abu Dhabi, which admits through NYU in New York on the American calendar.

deadlines.notes: Khalifa's undergraduate admissions page says Fall 2026 admissions are closed and, under the heading "Know the application timeline and deadlines", carries the single line "Stay tuned for the Fall 2027 application timeline". The university has not set a date yet. Check the page from autumn 2026. Admission is competitive and seat-limited, shortlisted applicants sit the Khalifa University Admission Test in person, and every applicant submits a video recording in place of an interview — so the working deadline is well before the stated one.

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: Where each UAE institution sits relative to this date matters. NYU Abu Dhabi closes eight months before it and decides on predicted grades. AUS wants a complete file the day before it. RIT Dubai's deadline falls seven weeks after it. Heriot-Watt Dubai will still take an application three weeks before term starts. The UAE is not one calendar, and treating it as one is how a student loses a year. On the date itself: 6 July is when results reach the candidate. 5 July, the day AUS wants a complete file, is also the IB's own transcript-request cut-off: before it your coordinator requests transcripts for you and the first six are free, after it you request them yourself at $19 each. steps: Work out which of the four admissions environments your institution is in before anything else. It decides the portal, the calendar, the entry rules and the degree you end up with.

For NYU Abu Dhabi, apply through the Common Application on the American timetable: Early Decision I on 1 November, Early Decision II on 1 January, Regular Decision on 5 January, all at 23:59 EST. Early Decision is binding. File the CSS Profile for financial aid alongside it — 10 November, 10 January or 1 February depending on the round.

For a branch campus, read the parent university’s entry requirements first. Birmingham Dubai states that it upholds the same entry requirements as its UK campus, and Heriot-Watt Dubai awards the same Scottish degree. Then apply through the UAE campus’s own portal, not through UCAS — a Dubai application does not use one of your five UCAS choices.

For a UAE private university — Khalifa, AUS, AUD, CUD — apply direct on its own calendar. These are the institutions whose 2027 dates are least likely to be published yet, so diarise a check for autumn 2026.

For a federal institution — UAEU, Zayed — check first whether the international stream is open to you at all. Places and subsidies are directed at UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers, who apply through a national placement route you cannot use.

Have every foreign certificate attested and equivalenced by the UAE Ministry of Education. Khalifa and RIT Dubai both make this an explicit condition, and the process is slow. Start it long before you have an offer.
Apply for financial aid at the same time as admission wherever the two are linked, not afterwards.

Once admitted, the university sponsors your student residence visa — you cannot arrange it yourself. Allow for a medical fitness test and an Emirates ID on arrival, and note that some institutions set a visa deadline weeks before term that is harder than the application deadline.
Sort accommodation through the university; most of the Abu Dhabi institutions house undergraduates on campus.
application.selectionNotes: Selection does not mean the same thing in the four environments. NYU Abu Dhabi assesses holistically on the American model with essays, references and a candidate weekend, and admitted 5% of applicants for autumn 2022 entry. Khalifa screens against published minimums, shortlists, then requires its own admission test in person and a video recording in place of an interview. The Dubai branch campuses apply the parent university’s published entry requirements and are generally accessible to a solid IB student. The federal institutions select within each college’s capacity and prioritise Emirati nationals ahead of everyone else.

tuitionEuEea.value: The UAE does not differentiate by nationality in the way Europe does. Most private institutions charge the same fee to everyone; federal institutions prioritise or subsidise Emirati nationals.

tuitionNonEu.value: NYU Abu Dhabi 2026-27: tuition USD 68,574, housing USD 6,000, food USD 5,800, total direct costs USD 84,520 including books and mandatory health insurance, total cost of attendance USD 90,434 including personal expenses and transportation. Khalifa University charges AED 2,500 per credit hour (roughly AED 81,250 a year); other fees are not given here, so check each institution's own page.

notes: NYUAD's sticker price is high and its aid is need-based, so read the aid policy before the fee. It does not state on its current pages that it meets full need, so ask what your CSS Profile would produce.
NYUAD states that annual adjustments to costs and fees should be expected, so budget above the 2026-27 figures for a 2027 start.
Branch campus fees in Dubai are typically a fraction of the home campus fee in the UK or Australia — but so is the subsidy, so compare the total net cost, not the headline.
The UAE has no income tax, which matters if you plan to work after graduating, but living costs in Dubai and Abu Dhabi are high: rent, car or taxi dependence, and air conditioning.

funding: NYU Abu Dhabi need-based aid. All financial aid grants offered by NYUAD to non-Emirati citizens are need-based, and the university also offers personal support awards. The only named merit scholarship is the Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship, which is restricted to admitted UAE nationals and children of an Emirati parent. Apply for aid at the same time as admission.

Khalifa University offers merit-based scholarships that can cover tuition, textbooks and accommodation, considered from the admission application with no separate form. Whether international students receive them on the same terms is not stated.
American University of Sharjah runs merit scholarships including the Sheikh Khalifa Scholarships, which recognise academic excellence and leadership. Ask AUS for the amounts.
Branch campuses generally offer modest merit discounts rather than full funding. Do not expect a European-style free place.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: Part-time work is restricted on a student residence visa — see 'Living there' below. It is not a funding strategy.
workRights: Students on a university-sponsored residence visa may work part-time with a permit, with rules that differ between the mainland and the free zones and have been liberalised in recent years. Confirm the current rules with the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship and with your university before relying on it.
residency: EU citizenship gives no advantage. EU/EEA citizens receive a visa on arrival as visitors, but you cannot study on that. Your university sponsors a student residence visa, which involves a medical fitness test (including a chest X-ray and blood test) and an Emirates ID. The visa is tied to the institution: if you leave the university, the visa is cancelled. Some students qualify for the UAE's five-year student 'golden visa' for outstanding academic performance.
housing: NYU Abu Dhabi, Khalifa and the American University of Sharjah all house undergraduates on campus, which is the simplest and safest arrangement. Dubai branch campuses vary: some have student accommodation in Dubai International Academic City or Knowledge Village, others expect you to rent privately. Private renting in Dubai usually means paying rent in a small number of large cheques up front, which is hard to manage as a first-year student.
healthcare: Health insurance is legally mandatory for residents in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, and universities normally include a compulsory scheme in the fees — NYUAD lists mandatory health insurance inside its direct costs. Healthcare is private, modern and expensive without cover. Your EHIC does not apply.

Early Decision at NYU Abu Dhabi is binding: an admitted student with an adequate financial aid package must withdraw other applications and accept within two to three weeks, and is released from the agreement only if the aid package will not let them attend.

notes: Every date on this route is provisional. NYUAD publishes its deadlines as bare recurring days with no year, so the years here are inferred for 2027 entry and must be confirmed against the Key Dates and Deadlines page before anyone acts on them. Early Decision I is the urgent one: on the inferred date it falls on 1 November 2026, five weeks after this record was written.

This route exists separately from the other three UAE routes because NYU Abu Dhabi does not admit on the UAE calendar at all. It is the clearest example in this Destination of a branch campus admitting through the parent institution's own system, on the parent's timetable.

systems.name: The Common Application (NYU Abu Dhabi)

jurisdiction.authority: The Common Application, on behalf of New York University
jurisdiction.area: One institution in the UAE: NYU Abu Dhabi. This record describes only that use of it.

coverage.includes: NYU Abu Dhabi, which is admitted to as one of NYU's three degree-granting campuses alongside New York and Shanghai.
coverage.excludes: Every other institution in the United Arab Emirates. Nothing else in this Destination uses it, and no UAE institution accepts an application made through it to another university.

choiceRules.note: The Common Application is not a ranked national portal. Each institution decides independently and a student may hold several offers — except where a binding Early Decision agreement has been signed, which removes that freedom by design.

systems.identityRequirement: A Common Application account. Financial aid is assessed separately through the CSS Profile, which is a second account with a second deadline.
systems.decisionModel: Holistic review on the American model — transcript and predicted grades, essays, references and interview — with three rounds, two of them binding. Decisions are released on fixed dates rather than as applications are read.
systems.replyModel: An Early Decision admit must withdraw other applications and accept within two to three weeks, and is released only if the financial aid package will not let them attend. Regular Decision admits reply on the American calendar.

notes: Recorded under the UAE because it is the application system one UAE institution uses, not because it is a UAE system. Its coverage field says so: within this Destination it covers exactly one university out of fourteen, which is the point worth making rather than a limitation of the record.
The rules on the Common Application's other member institutions are outside the scope of this record and are not established here.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: The UAE imports its universities. Dubai's academic free zones host British, Australian, Indian and American campuses awarding their home degrees; Abu Dhabi hosts NYU and the Sorbonne; and alongside them sit two federal universities built for Emirati nationals and a handful of UAE-owned private institutions awarding their own. Teaching is in English almost everywhere and the IB is read as a matter of routine. What is not routine is the calendar, because there is no calendar — there is no national admissions authority, no central portal and no shared deadline, and the four kinds of institution admit on four different timetables months apart. NYU Abu Dhabi closes on 1 November for the following autumn and decides on predicted grades. RIT Dubai will take an application on 22 August. Heriot-Watt Dubai will take one three weeks before term starts. Knowing which of those four you are dealing with is the whole skill of applying here.
